abstract: We report an experimental demonstration of a one-way implementation of a quantum algorithm solving Simon’s Problem - a black box period-finding problem which has an exponential gap between the classical and quantum runtime. Using an all-optical setup and modifying the bases of single-qubit measurements on a five-qubit cluster state, key representative functions of the logical two-qubit version’s black box can be queried and solved. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first experimental realization of the quantum algorithm solving Simon’s Problem. The experimental results are in excellent agreement with the theoretical model, demonstrating the successful performance of the algorithm. With a view to scaling up to larger numbers of qubits, we analyze the resource requirements for an $n$-qubit version. This work helps highlight how one-way quantum computing provides a practical route to experimentally investigating the quantum-classical gap in the query complexity model.

specification.problem: Solve Simon's Problem for a logical two-qubit black-box function f:{0,1}^2->{0,1}^2 with hidden period s (f(x)=f(y) iff y=x or y=x XOR s), using a one-way (measurement-based) implementation on a five-qubit photonic cluster state, with single-qubit measurement bases adapted to query representative functions.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Small finite instance: n=2 logical qubits Simon algorithm on a five-qubit cluster state; the abstract does not give the cluster geometry, measurement angles, or the specific functions. The n-qubit resource analysis is out of scope.

symbols.meaning: Black-box function promised to be two-to-one with hidden period s
Measured output string of the input register

equations.label: Simon promise
equations.description: Defines the hidden period of the black-box function.
equations.justification: Standard definition of Simon's Problem; the abstract only names a period-finding black-box problem.
assumptions: Two-to-one promise with s nonzero, or one-to-one for s=0

equations.label: Orthogonality condition
equations.description: Each measured string y is orthogonal to s; collecting independent y's determines s.
equations.justification: Standard Simon's algorithm output property, not stated in the abstract.

registers.name: cluster_input
registers.role: Logical input register x, ends up measured to give y

registers.name: cluster_aux
registers.role: Fifth cluster qubit; role not specified in abstract

specification.initial_state: Five-qubit photonic cluster state (graph geometry not given in abstract); logical registers assumed initialised in |+> via the cluster.

steps.description: Choose single-qubit measurement bases on the cluster qubits to implement the black-box oracle for a representative function f (the Simon promise).
Measure remaining qubits in bases that realise the final Hadamard-type step, yielding output string y satisfying the orthogonality condition.

specification.measurement: Single-qubit projective measurements of the photonic cluster qubits, with bases set per function (angles not given in the abstract). Outcomes of the qubits carrying the logical input register give the string y; the other qubits' outcomes are byproduct or output information (assumed).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Repeat runs to collect independent y strings satisfying y.s=0 mod 2 and solve the linear system over GF(2) for s. For n=2, a nonzero y fixes s, and y=00 gives no information. Compare outcome distributions with the theoretical model (assumed).
assumptions: Standard Simon's algorithm relations are used as background
Register sizes and roles are assumed, as the abstract only states five qubits and two logical qubits
Register split 2 input + 2 output + 1 auxiliary is assumed
Measurement readout and postprocessing follow the standard Simon algorithm
Measurement outcomes of the input-register qubits yield y; postprocessing is the standard GF(2) solve
missing_information: Cluster state graph and qubit roles
Actual mapping of the five physical qubits to logical registers
Which physical qubits are read out for y and how byproduct corrections are applied
